data.gender_notes: Renatia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'renatus', meaning 'reborn' or 'renewed'. In Christian tradition, it can also be derived from the name Regina, meaning 'queen'. The name Renatia carries the meaning “Reborn, Renewed” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Renatia usually hope their child will grow to embody reborn, renewed and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes new beginnings and a fresh start in life.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Renatia total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Renatia carries a deep cultural roots in Christianity, associated with the idea of rebirth and renewal. In many Christian communities, the name Renatia may be given to children born after a loss or a long struggle, symbolizing new life and hope. Moreover, it is often associated with the character of the Virgin Mary, who is believed to be the mother of Jesus Christ and a symbol of new life herself, in Roman Catholic tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Renatia holds deep spiritual significance in Christianity. From a theological standpoint, it serves as a constant reminder of the Christian doctrine of Rebirth, or the transformation and renewal of an individual's soul. In a more personal and individual sense, the name can be seen as a testimony of God's grace and mercy, offering comfort and hope in times of hardship and difficulties. It is a name that reflects the inherent belief in the power of redemption, forgiveness, and new beginnings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Renatia signifies rebirth and renewal in the Christian faith. This name is derived from the Latin word 'renatus,' meaning 'reborn.' It is a reminder of the transformative power of God in our lives, inviting us to embrace new beginnings and leave our old selves behind.
